Sweet Tamales for Candlemas

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Makes about 18-20 tamalesPrep 45 minCook 1 hour 15 min

Candlemas, or Día de la Candelaria, on February 2nd, marks the presentation of Jesus at the Temple and the purification of the Virgin Mary. In Mexico, it's a beloved tradition to celebrate with tamales, often hosted by the person who found the baby Jesus figurine in the Rosca de Reyes on Epiphany. Sweet tamales, with their delightful hint of sugar and fruit, are a festive and comforting way to honor this day, bringing warmth and community to the winter celebration.

Ingredients

  • 30-40 dried corn husks
  • 2.5 cups (300g) masa harina for tamales
  • 1 cup (225g) lard or vegetable shortening, at room temperature
  • 3/4 cup (150g) granulated sugar
  • 1 tablespoon (15g) baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5g) salt
  • 2 cups (480ml) warm water or milk, plus more if needed
  • 1 teaspoon (5ml) vanilla extract
  • 1 teaspoon (5g) ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 cup (75g) raisins, optional

Method

  1. Place corn husks in a large bowl or pot, cover with very hot water, and weigh down with a plate to keep them submerged. Let them soak for at least 30 minutes, or until pliable. Drain and pat dry before using.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, using an electric mixer, beat the lard or shortening until light and fluffy, about 3-5 minutes.
  3. Gradually add the granulated sugar to the lard, beating until well combined and fluffy, about 2-3 minutes more.
  4. In a separate bowl, whisk together the masa harina, baking powder, salt, and ground cinnamon.
  5. Gradually add the dry masa mixture to the creamed lard mixture, alternating with the warm water or milk, beginning and ending with the masa mixture. Add the vanilla extract.
  6. Continue beating the masa dough for about 10-15 minutes, until it is very light, fluffy, and resembles a thick cake batter. To test if it's ready, drop a small 1/2 teaspoon of dough into a glass of cold water; if it floats, it's ready. If it sinks, continue beating for a few more minutes and retest.
  7. To assemble the tamales, take one softened corn husk, place it with the wider end at the top. Spread about 2-3 tablespoons of masa dough evenly over the wider part of the husk, leaving about 1 inch (2.5 cm) clear at the top and sides.
  8. If using, sprinkle a small amount of raisins down the center of the masa.
  9. Fold one long side of the husk over the filling, then fold the other long side over to overlap. Fold the narrow bottom end of the husk up towards the center. Leave the top open.
  10. Repeat with the remaining masa and corn husks.
  11. Arrange the tamales upright (open-end up) in a steamer basket. If you don't have a steamer, you can use a large pot with a colander or a metal rack at the bottom, ensuring the water level is below the tamales.
  12. Pour about 2-3 inches (5-7.5 cm) of water into the bottom of the steamer or pot. Bring the water to a boil, then reduce heat to a steady simmer. Cover tightly with a lid.
  13. Steam the tamales for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, or until the masa easily separates from the corn husk. You may need to add more hot water to the pot during steaming if it evaporates too quickly.
  14. Carefully remove tamales from the steamer and let them rest for 5-10 minutes before serving. This allows them to firm up slightly.

Tips

  • For an extra fruity flavor, you can add 1/4 cup (60g) of finely diced candied fruit or finely chopped dried pineapple to the masa dough.
  • Ensure your masa dough is very light and fluffy; this is key to tender tamales. The 'float test' is a reliable indicator.
  • Tamales can be made ahead of time and refrigerated for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 2 months. Reheat by steaming or microwaving until warmed through.
